inputs.text: I’m wary of calling tighter rules for Nigerians and others a “necessary reminder.” That framing treats people seeking safety as a threat to public order, while ignoring how easily immigration enforcement can deepen racialized exclusion. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026, but a law being enacted doesn’t make its consequences fair. Canada can manage its borders without turning asylum into suspicion or making vulnerable people pay for political claims about disorder. Public trust depends on a system that protects people’s rights, not just one that enforces restrictions.
